policy_title: Introduce NHS voucher scheme for waiting lists
stated: Reform UK will introduce an NHS voucher scheme where patients receive a voucher for private treatment if they cannot see a GP within 3 days, a consultant within 3 weeks, or have an operation within 9 weeks. Services will remain free at the point of use.

source.quote: Put Patients in Charge With a New NHS Voucher Scheme NHS Patients will receive a voucher for private treatment if they can’t see a GP within 3 days. For a consultant it would be 3 weeks. For an operation, 9 weeks. Services will always be free at the point of use.

bearing_set.reason: The policy directly targets NHS waiting times for GPs, consultants, and operations — the core access and capacity indicators of O3 — by redirecting patients to private care when thresholds are breached, earning a real verdict on whether treatment access improves or worsens.

Vouchers funded from public money for all patients breaching thresholds would constitute a large, potentially open-ended spending commitment whose fiscal sustainability is a non-negligible public-finances question.

Private hospital capacity is geographically concentrated (typically in wealthier areas) and NHS staff may migrate to the private sector, creating a credible mechanism by which the scheme's benefits distribute unevenly across income and regional groups — a real inequality effect.

membership_note: Three fundamentals earn real verdicts: O3 (the primary access target), O12 (fiscal cost of vouchers at scale), and O14 (distributional access to private providers and NHS staffing effects). O11 is not directly implicated (no tax-rate change). O13 (productivity) is too indirect given no specific mechanism cited.
